messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1998765432 - continuous-batcher pool degradation in us-west-2. Symptoms: repeated GPU OOMs, container restarts, extreme latency. Pager: oncall-alex. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/continuous-batcher
oncall-alex: Ack, I'm on it. Seeing 95th latency > 20s for /generate, elevated 5xx. Kicking off log collection and pod list.
sre-maya: Looking at node metrics — node-17-gpu is paging heavily and showing oom_kill events. Kernel excerpt:```kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 21453 (python) total-vm=5123456kB, anon-rss=4200000kB, file-rss=0kB```Also NVML logs show repeated device reset: `NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus` and `nvml: driver has been unloaded`.
eng-runtime-jun: We rolled batcher v2.4 ~12m ago; it included the new dynamic-aggregation changes (removed backpressure cap). Suspect unbounded batch growth under a burst of long chats. Can we flip the feature flag?
incident-bot: Suggested mitigations from runbook: 1) reduce max-batch-size 2) restart affected nodes 3) scale down continuous-batcher replicas 4) enable fallback to low-latency model variant.
carla-support: Customers reporting: Acme (enterprise), Nova Labs, WidgetCorp seeing timeouts starting ~10:03 PDT. Error says 502 / 504. I'm escalating to their CSMs.
ben-sales: Are Dedicated customers affected?
carla-support: Dedicated tenants on isolated pools unaffected. This is hosted us-west-2 continuous-batcher pool only.
oncall-alex: Immediate plan: cordon + drain node-17-gpu, scale continuous-batcher to 1 replica to break pending queue, and roll a config change to limit pending batch queue length. Executing now.
ops-derek: Node-17 has massive kswapd CPU and huge page-in/out counts. I'm going to swapoff -a on that host to stop swap thrash and reboot if needed. Command:```ssh ops@node-17 sudo swapoff -a && sudo systemctl reboot```
sre-maya: Also doing a hot-patch: set env BATCHER_MAX_PENDING=200 on the deployment and restart the pods in canary. Command:```kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher BATCHER_MAX_PENDING=200 --namespace=prod && kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod --selector=canary=true```
eng-ml-tara: Observed that KV cache size grows without eviction for long conversations; continuous-batcher accumulates KV per request and aggregation ties multiple requests into a single large KV set. Need LRU eviction and hard limit on KV bytes.
eva-qa: I'm watching synthetic traffic against the canary. Sending long prompt sequences to reproduce. Initial result: canary at 10% saw no OOMs after BATCHER_MAX_PENDING change.
danny: Noted repeated stderr message in pod logs:```Traceback (most recent call last): MemoryError``` and `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in some stacks. Suggests device resets while Python in middle of batch work.
eng-runtime-jun: Patch looks promising. I'll keep canary at 10% for 15m then ramp if stable. Also adding temporary guard: if pending queued requests > 500, reject new requests with 429 and priority fallback.
carla-support: Notifying affected customers: Acme ticket updated, Nova on call. Sending status update in 10m.
sre-maya: After drain + swapoff + canary, node-17 telemetry shows memory pressure dropping and no further oom_kill in the last 5m. GPU resets decreased but driver WARN still present on one host; planning driver restart during maintenance window.
oncall-alex: Live rollback path if canary degrades: flip feature-flag dynamic-aggregation=false. I have runbook steps ready.
incident-bot: Update: mitigation steps executed: node drain, swapoff, BATCHER_MAX_PENDING=200, canary rollout. Monitoring for 30m.
eng-runtime-jun: Canary at 10% -> 100% over 12m with no OOMs. Rolling to full. Also added temporary healthcheck: fail if pending_count > 1000 to avoid silent buildup.
sre-maya: Post-mitigation checks: 95th latency dropped from 22s to 1.6s, error rate down to baseline. Marking immediate impact mitigated.
oncall-alex: Post-incident actions: 1) revert dynamic-aggregation until we add KV eviction; 2) add telemetry for per-pool pending_batch_count and kv_cache_bytes; 3) enforce cgroup limit checks in autoscaler; 4) schedule driver upgrade for nodes with NVML warnings.
eng-ml-tara: I'll work on LRU eviction and a hard byte cap for KV cache. Expect PR in 48h.
sre-maya: Drafting postmortem notes. Preliminary root cause: regression in continuous-batcher aggregation logic removed backpressure cap, combined with long-conversation KV growth. Under burst load this allowed memory usage to exceed container/cgroup limits, triggering OOMs and cascading into GPU driver resets and container restarts. Secondary contributor: swap configured on GPUs caused severe paging under memory pressure -> swap thrash.
danny: Adding to postmortem: add test harness that simulates long prompts + burst patterns to surface aggregation regressions.
carla-support: Sent final update to customers: mitigation applied, latency restored, will follow up with RCA.
ben-sales: Thanks everyone — letting the sales CSMs know we have a remediation plan.
ops-derek: Nodes 17/19 rebooted, kernel logs show no further OOMs. Planning to re-enable swap only with strict limits; prefer no swap on GPU nodes.
eva-qa: Regression test added to CI to block dynamic-aggregation without guarded limits.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1998765432 status: RESOLVED (mitigated, follow-ups assigned). Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1998765432.
oncall-alex: Closing loop here — service healthy, monitoring green. Scheduling a post-mortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 PDT. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
